section: Nuclear energy - three-stage programme, types of reactors, PHWR/FBR/AHWR, thorium strategy
subsections: Fast breeder reactors - principle, PFBR, milestones
Research and advanced reactors - type and location

accepted.s: The Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor (PFBR) at Kalpakkam was built and commissioned by which organisation?
o: Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited
accepted.x: BHAVINI built and commissioned the 500 MWe PFBR at Kalpakkam. The reactor was designed by IGCAR.
accepted.tq: Identify the organisation directly associated with construction and commissioning.
accepted.sec: Fast breeder reactors - principle, PFBR, milestones  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to the PFBR at Kalpakkam, consider the following statements:
1. It is a sodium-cooled reactor.
2. It is of the pool type.
3. Its rated electrical capacity is 500 MWe and thermal capacity is 1,250 MWt.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The PFBR is sodium-cooled and pool-type, with a capacity of 500 MWe and 1,250 MWt. Therefore, all three statements are correct.
accepted.tq: Split the options by checking the reactor’s coolant, design and capacity.
accepted.sec: Fast breeder reactors - principle, PFBR, milestones  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following milestones relating to the PFBR in chronological order:
A. Beginning of work on the reactor
B. Core loading in the presence of the Prime Minister
C. First criticality

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Work began in 2004, core loading took place on 4 March 2024, and first criticality was achieved in April 2026.
accepted.tq: Use the dates to establish the first, middle and last milestones.
accepted.sec: Fast breeder reactors - principle, PFBR, milestones  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The first criticality of the PFBR at Kalpakkam was achieved in:
accepted.x: The PFBR achieved first criticality in April 2026; the announcement was made on 6 April 2026.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the date of criticality from the earlier date of core loading.
accepted.sec: Fast breeder reactors - principle, PFBR, milestones  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Once the PFBR operates commercially, India is expected to become the second country after which country to operate a commercial-scale fast breeder reactor?
accepted.x: India is expected to become the second country after Russia to operate a commercial-scale fast breeder reactor.
accepted.tq: Use the country comparison and identify the stated predecessor.
accepted.sec: Fast breeder reactors - principle, PFBR, milestones  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the PFBR project:
1. Its final cost was ₹8,181 crore.
2. Its final cost was more than twice the sanctioned cost.
3. Its first criticality occurred more than sixteen years later than originally scheduled.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The final cost was ₹8,181 crore, exceeding twice the sanctioned amount, and criticality was delayed by more than sixteen years. Hence, all three statements are correct.
accepted.tq: Check the numerical figure together with the two project-delay comparisons.
accepted.sec: Fast breeder reactors - principle, PFBR, milestones  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The fast-reactor fuel-cycle facility associated with the PFBR is due to be completed by:
accepted.x: The fast-reactor fuel-cycle facility is scheduled to be completed by 2029.
accepted.tq: Test the specific completion year rather than the reactor’s commissioning year.
accepted.sec: Fast breeder reactors - principle, PFBR, milestones  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Before the PFBR can commence commercial operation, which authority must clear its low-power tests?
o: Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited
accepted.x: The Atomic Energy Regulatory Board (AERB) must clear the PFBR’s low-power tests before commercial operation begins.
accepted.tq: Apply the ‘who would do this job?’ method to regulatory approval.
accepted.sec: Fast breeder reactors - principle, PFBR, milestones  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly compares fuel use and burn-up in PHWRs and fast breeder reactors?
o: PHWRs use about 1% fuel and FBRs about 10% or more; burn-up can rise from about 8,000 to about 1,00,000 units
PHWRs use about 1% fuel and FBRs about 10% or more; burn-up falls from about 1,00,000 to about 8,000 units
PHWRs use about 10% fuel and FBRs about 1%; burn-up falls to about 8,000 units
Both PHWRs and FBRs use about 1% fuel; burn-up remains around 8,000 units
accepted.x: Fuel use is about 1% in PHWRs and about 10% or more in FBRs. Burn-up is expected to increase from approximately 8,000 to 1,00,000 units.
accepted.tq: Check both sides of the comparison and watch for reversed figures and trends.
accepted.sec: Fast breeder reactors - principle, PFBR, milestones  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Following a performance review of the PFBR, what further project is planned at Kalpakkam?
o: Two 500 MWe FBRs, designated FBR 1 and 2
accepted.x: After a year-long performance review, two additional 500 MWe fast breeder reactors, FBR 1 and FBR 2, are planned at Kalpakkam.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the planned follow-up project by number, capacity and reactor type.
accepted.sec: Fast breeder reactors - principle, PFBR, milestones  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The 2005 milestone associated with IGCAR and the Fast Breeder Test Reactor was:
accepted.x: IGCAR’s 2005 milestone was the reprocessing of the mixed-carbide fuel used in the Fast Breeder Test Reactor.
accepted.tq: Match the institution and year with the specific technological achievement.
accepted.sec: Fast breeder reactors - principle, PFBR, milestones  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Dhruva — Trombay — India’s largest research reactor
accepted.x: Dhruva is located at Trombay and is India’s largest research reactor. KAMINI is at Kalpakkam, while APSARA and CIRUS are at Trombay.
accepted.tq: Find the sure location-and-identity pair before checking the other matches.
accepted.sec: Research and advanced reactors - type and location  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to APSARA, consider the following statements:
1. It is located at BARC, Trombay.
2. It became critical in 1956.
3. It was the first research reactor of India and Asia.
4. It is a swimming-pool or pool-type reactor.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: APSARA is a pool-type reactor at Trombay that became critical in 1956 and was India’s and Asia’s first research reactor. All four statements are correct.
accepted.tq: Verify each statement against the reactor’s location, date, status and design.
accepted.sec: Research and advanced reactors - type and location  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about CIRUS is NOT correct?
o: It was used for research and plutonium-239 production.
It is moderated by heavy water.
It has continued operation after 2010 without interruption.
accepted.x: CIRUS was shut down in 2010. It was a 40 MW heavy-water-moderated, natural-uranium reactor used for research and plutonium-239 production.
accepted.tq: Find the statement that conflicts with the reactor’s shutdown status.
accepted.sec: Research and advanced reactors - type and location  [APPSC]

accepted.s: CIRUS was built with the assistance of which country, following a decision taken in 1956?
accepted.x: CIRUS was built with Canadian assistance; the decision to build it was taken in 1956.
accepted.tq: Separate the foreign collaboration detail from the reactor’s location and purpose.
accepted.sec: Research and advanced reactors - type and location  [APPSC]

accepted.s: KAMINI is distinguished from the other research reactors in India because it is:
o: The world’s only operating reactor fuelled by U-233
India’s first pool-type research reactor using natural uranium
A 300 MW thorium reactor using boiling heavy water
accepted.x: KAMINI at Kalpakkam is a 30 kW reactor fuelled by U-233 and is described as the world’s only operating U-233 reactor.
accepted.tq: Discriminate KAMINI from APSARA, Dhruva and AHWR by its unique fuel.
accepted.sec: Research and advanced reactors - type and location  [APPSC]

accepted.s: KAMINI is primarily associated with which application?
o: Production of plutonium-239 from natural uranium
Operation as a fast reactor without coolant
accepted.x: KAMINI is used for neutron radiography of irradiated fuel. It is a 30 kW U-233-fuelled reactor at Kalpakkam.
accepted.tq: Identify the application linked to the reactor’s distinctive technical role.
accepted.sec: Research and advanced reactors - type and location  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the AHWR?
o: A 500 MWe sodium-cooled fast breeder reactor using only plutonium
A 300 MW thorium reactor with heavy-water moderator and boiling light-water coolant
A 30 kW U-233 reactor used for neutron radiography
A 40 MW natural-uranium reactor moderated by heavy water and shut down in 2010
accepted.x: The AHWR is a 300 MW thorium reactor designed by BARC, using a heavy-water moderator, boiling light-water coolant and a Th-232 plus U-233 fuel combination.
accepted.tq: Match the reactor’s capacity, fuel strategy, moderator and coolant together.
accepted.sec: Research and advanced reactors - type and location  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List-I (Reactor)
 a. APSARA
 b. CIRUS
 c. KAMINI
 d. Dhruva

List-II (Characteristic)
 i. 30 kW U-233-fuelled reactor
 ii. India’s largest research reactor
 iii. Asia’s first research reactor
 iv. Natural uranium and heavy-water moderation

Select the correct code.
accepted.x: APSARA was Asia’s first research reactor; CIRUS used natural uranium and heavy-water moderation; KAMINI is the 30 kW U-233 reactor; Dhruva is India’s largest research reactor.
accepted.tq: Start from the distinctive KAMINI and Dhruva pairs, then complete the remaining matches.
accepted.sec: Research and advanced reactors - type and location  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: AHWR — reactor already built and operating at Trombay
accepted.x: AHWR is a BARC design for a 300 MW thorium reactor; it is not described as an already built and operating reactor at Trombay. The other pairs are correct.
accepted.tq: Reject the option that changes a design-stage reactor into an operating facility.
accepted.sec: Research and advanced reactors - type and location  [APPSC]
